q: This paper presents an experience report originating from a three-day hackathon held in June 2026[14], whose theme was the construction of materials databases using AI agents.
r: Include: experience report of building and hardening a full application with a coding agent, project level; kept as borderline.

q: For evaluation, we construct checklists for turn-wise constraint compliance and final functional correctness, integrating verification scripts and judge agents to ensure evaluation reliability.
r: Include: new benchmark for instruction-following (repository policy files, constraints) of coding agents in multi-turn software development.

q: We introduce ProgramDistill, comprising 4,063 replayverified SWE tasks derived from 1,975 behaviors across 26 interactive web applications, spanning atomic repair, cumulative repair, and full-application reconstruction.
r: Include: new benchmark whose tasks include full-application reconstruction, a contribution to evaluation, borderline against issue repair.

q: We propose the first trajectory-aware subset selection approach for SWE-agent regression testing that combines deterministic geometric selection with historical outcome grouping over sanitized trajectory embeddings.
r: EC6: evaluation cost reduction on SWE-Bench Verified and SWE-Rebench, i.e. issue repair, which is always excluded.

q: Constructed tasks reproduce the mechanism on 12 Django helpers, with 97% interference and 82% recovery using an oracle message.
r: Include: new benchmark for coordination of parallel coding agents, evaluation method contribution; short workshop paper (6 pages) is kept.

q: AsynCodeBench studies this challenge through repository-grounded dependencies, making collaboration and its evolution directly measurable during execution.
r: Include: new benchmark and metrics for asynchronous multi-agent repository-level software development.

q: Across 584 runs, we compare six agents on six open-weight model endpoints, run six agent-model pairings 52 times each under fixed settings, and repeat three of them on a larger model from the same family.
r: Include: main contribution is the evaluation method (intensive repetitions, compliance audits, cost) for coding agents and models.

q: Here we introduce ReviveBench, a benchmark with two task families evaluated by hidden verifiers calibrated against native execution environments, established engineering tools, or purpose-built reference implementations.
r: Include: new benchmark with code development tasks (restoring software, rebuilding engines from specifications) and a verifier audit.

q: We construct LOLBENCH, a multilingual benchmark that consists of 100 modular development tasks from enhancement proposals containing user intent and high-level design, across 29 large software systems in five domains.
r: Include: new benchmark of feature-level development tasks from enhancement proposals, 28 agent configurations.

q: Agents deliver complete repositories from an empty workspace; acceptance is sealed, deterministic, and all-or-nothing. The design is language-agnostic, and the current release covers Python, TypeScript, Go, C++, C, and Zig.
r: Include: new benchmark where agents build complete repositories from a product requirements document, project level.
